items.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: One of my favorite trumpet players, Joe Thomas, who is not known at all, Joe was black, he was playing with these guys

ctx.x: Is it political correctness gone amok?

Well of course. I mean and it’s a problem so that the consequence, as we were talking about the Dixieland stuff has been left out of jazz histories, why? Because it was mostly a white movement. There were plenty of blacks involved, sure. One of my favorite trumpet players, Joe Thomas, who is not known at all, Joe was black, he was playing with these guys, We know he was playing with these guys, there were others.
